knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE)

# 0. Setup

**Folder:** put this file in one folder together with

- `climate_panel.dta` and `AreaWeightedClimate.dta` (replication package, openICPSR 114251)
- the WDI CSV for `NY.GDP.PCAP.KN` (any file name starting with `API_NY`)

The CRU climate data are downloaded automatically in section 1 if `cru_country_year.csv` does not exist yet.

**Packages** (install once):
`install.packages(c("haven", "dplyr", "tidyr", "fixest", "countrycode", "ggplot2"))`

```{r packages}
library(haven)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(fixest)
library(countrycode)
library(ggplot2)

end_year <- 2024   # last year in the extension; 2025 GDP data are often incomplete

# Check that the input files are there
wdi_file <- list.files(".", pattern = "^API_NY.*GDP.*PCAP.*KN.*\\.csv$")[1]
needed   <- c("climate_panel.dta", "AreaWeightedClimate.dta")
stopifnot("Replication .dta files missing from this folder" = all(file.exists(needed)),
          "WDI CSV (API_NY...csv) missing from this folder" = !is.na(wdi_file))
cat("Working directory:", getwd(), "\nWDI file:", wdi_file, "\n")
```

# 1. Download the CRU-CY climate data

Downloads the CRU-CY v4.10 country files for temperature (`tmp`) and precipitation (`pre`), parses them and saves `cru_country_year.csv`. **Skipped automatically if that file already exists.** The first run takes a few minutes.

Source: Harris et al. (2020), *Scientific Data*, doi:10.1038/s41597-020-0453-3.

```{r cru-download}
read_per <- function(path) {
  hdr     <- readLines(path, n = 2)
  country <- trimws(sub(":.*", "", sub("^Country = ", "", hdr[2])))
  param   <- trimws(sub(":.*", "", sub(".*Parameter = ", "", hdr[2])))
  fname   <- basename(path)
  var <- if (grepl("tmp", fname, ignore.case = TRUE)) "tmp" else
         if (grepl("pre", fname, ignore.case = TRUE)) "pre" else
         if (grepl("temp", param, ignore.case = TRUE)) "tmp" else
         if (grepl("precip", param, ignore.case = TRUE)) "pre" else NA
  x <- read.table(path, skip = 3, header = TRUE, na.strings = "-999.0")
  data.frame(cru_name = country, var = var, year = x$YEAR, value = x$ANN)
}

if (!file.exists("cru_country_year.csv")) {
  base <- "https://crudata.uea.ac.uk/cru/data/hrg/cru_ts_4.10/crucy.2606161920.v4.10/countries/"
  dir.create("cru_files", showWarnings = FALSE)
  for (v in c("tmp", "pre")) {
    url   <- paste0(base, v, "/")
    html  <- readLines(url, warn = FALSE)
    files <- unique(regmatches(html, regexpr('[^"/>]+\\.per', html)))
    cat(v, ":", length(files), "files\n")
    for (f in files) {
      dest <- file.path("cru_files", f)
      if (!file.exists(dest)) download.file(paste0(url, f), dest, quiet = TRUE)
    }
  }
  paths <- list.files("cru_files", pattern = "\\.per$", full.names = TRUE)
  out   <- do.call(rbind, lapply(paths, read_per))
  write.csv(out, "cru_country_year.csv", row.names = FALSE)
}

cru <- read.csv("cru_country_year.csv")
table(cru$var)   # should be about 36,500 each
```

# 2. Replication of Table 2

R translation of `maketable2.do`.

## 2.1 Data preparation

```{r rep-data}
d <- read_dta("climate_panel.dta") |>
  filter(year <= 2003) |>                       # paper's sample ends in 2003
  arrange(fips60_06, year) |>
  group_by(fips60_06) |>
  mutate(
    # growth of GDP per capita (WDI, constant LCU) in %
    g   = ifelse(lag(year) == year - 1,
                 100 * (log(gdpLCU) - log(lag(gdpLCU))), NA),
    n_g = sum(!is.na(g))
  ) |>
  ungroup() |>
  filter(n_g >= 20)                             # at least 20 years of growth data

# "Poor" = below-median initial PPP GDP p.c. (one obs per country).
# The .do file takes ln() of lnrgdpl_t0 (log of a log); monotonic, so the split is unchanged.
ctry <- d |> filter(!is.na(lnrgdpl_t0)) |> distinct(fips60_06, .keep_all = TRUE)
med  <- quantile(ctry$lnrgdpl_t0, 0.5, type = 2)          # type 2 = Stata's xtile
ctry$poor <- as.integer(ctry$lnrgdpl_t0 <= med)

# "Hot" = above-median 1950s temperature (used in Table 2, column 4)
ctry_h <- d |> filter(!is.na(wtem50)) |> distinct(fips60_06, .keep_all = TRUE)
ctry_h$hot <- as.integer(ctry_h$wtem50 > quantile(ctry_h$wtem50, 0.5, type = 2))

regs <- c("_MENA", "_SSAF", "_LAC", "_WEOFF", "_EECA", "_SEAS")
d$region <- NA_character_
for (r in regs) d$region[d[[r]] == 1] <- r

d <- d |>
  left_join(select(ctry,   fips60_06, poor), by = "fips60_06") |>
  left_join(select(ctry_h, fips60_06, hot),  by = "fips60_06") |>
  mutate(region_year = paste0(region, year),
         wtem_poor = wtem * poor, wpre_poor = wpre * poor,
         wtem_hot  = wtem * hot,  wpre_hot  = wpre * hot)

est <- d |> filter(!is.na(g), !is.na(poor))
cat("Observations:", nrow(est), " Countries:", n_distinct(est$fips60_06),
    " Years:", min(est$year), "-", max(est$year), "\n")
```

## 2.2 Estimation

Fixed effects: country, region × year, poor × year. Standard errors two-way clustered by parent country and region × year (as `cgmreg` in the paper).

```{r rep-estimates}
cl <- ~ parent + region_year

m1 <- feols(g ~ wtem                                        | fips60_06 + region^year + poor^year, est, cluster = cl)
m2 <- feols(g ~ wtem + wtem_poor                            | fips60_06 + region^year + poor^year, est, cluster = cl)
m3 <- feols(g ~ wtem + wtem_poor + wpre + wpre_poor         | fips60_06 + region^year + poor^year, est, cluster = cl)
m4 <- feols(g ~ wtem + wtem_poor + wpre + wpre_poor +
                wtem_hot + wpre_hot                         | fips60_06 + region^year + poor^year, est, cluster = cl)

etable(m1, m2, m3, m4, digits = 3,
       signif.code = c("***" = .01, "**" = .05, "*" = .10),
       headers = c("(1)", "(2)", "(3)", "(4)"))
```

## 2.3 Effect in poor countries

β(temperature) + β(temperature × poor), the equivalent of Stata's `lincom`.

```{r poor-effect}
poor_effect <- function(m, v, suffix = "_poor") {
  b <- coef(m); V <- vcov(m); vp <- paste0(v, suffix)
  e  <- unname(b[v] + b[vp])
  se <- unname(sqrt(V[v, v] + V[vp, vp] + 2 * V[v, vp]))
  c(effect = e, se = se, p = 2 * pnorm(-abs(e / se)))
}

round(rbind(
  "Col 2, temperature"   = poor_effect(m2, "wtem"),
  "Col 3, temperature"   = poor_effect(m3, "wtem"),
  "Col 3, precipitation" = poor_effect(m3, "wpre"),
  "Col 4, temperature"   = poor_effect(m4, "wtem")
), 3)
```

## 2.4 Figure: poor vs. rich countries

```{r fig-effects}
fig <- data.frame(
  group = factor(c("Rich countries", "Poor countries"),
                 levels = c("Rich countries", "Poor countries")),
  est   = c(coef(m3)["wtem"], poor_effect(m3, "wtem")["effect"]),
  se    = c(se(m3)["wtem"],   poor_effect(m3, "wtem")["se"])
)

ggplot(fig, aes(group, est)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed") +
  geom_pointrange(aes(ymin = est - 1.96 * se, ymax = est + 1.96 * se), size = 0.8) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Effect of +1°C on annual growth (pp)",
       title = "Effect of a 1°C warmer year on economic growth",
       subtitle = "Table 2, column 3; 95% confidence intervals") +
  theme_minimal()
```

# 3. Robustness

## 3.1 Placebo: future temperature

Next year's temperature should not affect this year's growth. A significant lead would suggest a problem with the design.

```{r placebo}
est <- est |>
  arrange(fips60_06, year) |>
  group_by(fips60_06) |>
  mutate(wtem_lead = ifelse(lead(year) == year + 1, lead(wtem), NA)) |>
  ungroup() |>
  mutate(wtem_lead_poor = wtem_lead * poor)

m_lead <- feols(g ~ wtem + wtem_poor + wtem_lead + wtem_lead_poor |
                  fips60_06 + region^year + poor^year, est, cluster = cl)

round(rbind(
  "Contemporaneous temperature, poor" = poor_effect(m_lead, "wtem"),
  "Next year's temperature, poor"     = poor_effect(m_lead, "wtem_lead")
), 3)
```

## 3.2 Sensitivity to the data: temperature weighting and GDP vintage

Changing one input at a time, original period only:

- area-weighted instead of population-weighted temperature (the paper's own `AreaWeightedClimate.dta`)
- the current WDI vintage instead of the 2011 GDP data

```{r sensitivity}
# (a) area-weighted temperature
aw  <- read_dta("AreaWeightedClimate.dta")
est <- est |>
  left_join(aw, by = c("fips60_06", "year")) |>
  mutate(atem_poor = atem * poor, apre_poor = apre * poor)

m_aw <- feols(g ~ atem + atem_poor + apre + apre_poor |
                fips60_06 + region^year + poor^year, est, cluster = cl)

# (b) current WDI GDP vintage
w   <- read.csv(wdi_file, skip = 4, check.names = FALSE)
yrs <- grep("^[0-9]{4}$", names(w), value = TRUE)
wdi <- w |>
  select(iso3 = `Country Code`, all_of(yrs)) |>
  pivot_longer(-iso3, names_to = "year", values_to = "gdp_pc") |>
  mutate(year = as.integer(year)) |>
  filter(!is.na(gdp_pc), gdp_pc > 0) |>
  arrange(iso3, year) |>
  group_by(iso3) |>
  mutate(g_new = ifelse(lag(year) == year - 1,
                        100 * (log(gdp_pc) - log(lag(gdp_pc))), NA)) |>
  ungroup()

est <- est |>
  mutate(iso3 = recode(country_code, ROM = "ROU", ZAR = "COD")) |>
  left_join(select(wdi, iso3, year, g_new), by = c("iso3", "year"))

m_wdi <- feols(g_new ~ wtem + wtem_poor + wpre + wpre_poor |
                 fips60_06 + region^year + poor^year, est, cluster = cl)

round(rbind(
  "Paper (pop-weighted temp, 2011 WDI)"   = poor_effect(m3,    "wtem"),
  "Area-weighted temp, 2011 WDI"          = poor_effect(m_aw,  "atem"),
  "Pop-weighted temp, current WDI"        = poor_effect(m_wdi, "wtem")
), 3)
```

# 4. Extension: new data up to `r end_year`

## 4.1 Country definitions from the paper

Poor/rich, region and parent country are taken from the paper, so only the data change. Romania (ROM → ROU) and DR Congo (ZAR → COD) changed codes; Yugoslavia drops out.

```{r ext-info}
info <- ctry |>
  mutate(region = NA_character_)
for (r in regs) info$region[info[[r]] == 1] <- r
info <- info |>
  transmute(fips60_06, parent, region, poor,
            iso3 = recode(country_code, ROM = "ROU", ZAR = "COD"))
cat("Paper countries:", nrow(info), " poor:", sum(info$poor), "\n")
```

## 4.2 Match CRU country names to ISO3 codes

Check the unmatched names: if one of the paper's countries is among them, add it to `custom_match`, e.g. `c("CRU name" = "ISO")`.

```{r ext-cru}
# CRU writes names with underscores ("South_Korea") and has a few typos
cru$iso3 <- countrycode(gsub("_", " ", cru$cru_name), "country.name", "iso3c",
                        warn = FALSE,
                        custom_match = c("Vanatu" = "VUT", "Puerto Rica" = "PRI",
                                         "St Lucia" = "LCA",
                                         "Bassas da India" = NA))   # French islet, not India

# Safety check: each ISO3 code must come from exactly one CRU name
# (otherwise an island file would be averaged with the mainland). Should be empty.
dups <- cru |> filter(!is.na(iso3)) |> distinct(iso3, cru_name) |>
  group_by(iso3) |> filter(n() > 1) |> arrange(iso3)
dups

unmatched <- sort(unique(cru$cru_name[is.na(cru$iso3)]))
cat("Unmatched CRU names (", length(unmatched), "):\n", sep = ""); print(unmatched)

cru_w <- cru |>
  filter(!is.na(iso3)) |>
  group_by(iso3, year, var) |>
  summarise(value = mean(value, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = var, values_from = value) |>
  transmute(iso3, year, tem = tmp, pre = pre / 100)   # pre in 100s of mm/year, as in the paper

cat("Paper countries without CRU data:", setdiff(info$iso3, cru_w$iso3), "\n")
```

## 4.3 Build the new panel

```{r ext-panel}
new <- wdi |>
  transmute(iso3, year, g = g_new) |>
  inner_join(info,  by = "iso3") |>
  inner_join(cru_w, by = c("iso3", "year")) |>
  filter(year <= end_year) |>
  mutate(region_year = paste0(region, year),
         tem_poor = tem * poor, pre_poor = pre * poor)

cat("New panel:", n_distinct(new$iso3), "countries,",
    min(new$year), "-", max(new$year), "\n")
```

## 4.4 Do CRU and the paper's temperature agree?

Within-country correlation (each country's mean removed) with the paper's area-weighted temperature, the same weighting as CRU-CY.

```{r ext-compare}
cmp <- new |>
  select(iso3, year, tem) |>
  inner_join(aw |> inner_join(select(info, fips60_06, iso3), by = "fips60_06") |>
               select(iso3, year, atem),
             by = c("iso3", "year")) |>
  filter(!is.na(tem), !is.na(atem)) |>
  group_by(iso3) |>
  mutate(tem_dm = tem - mean(tem), atem_dm = atem - mean(atem)) |>
  ungroup()

cat("Within-country correlation, CRU vs paper (area-weighted):",
    round(cor(cmp$tem_dm, cmp$atem_dm), 3), "\n")
```

## 4.5 Results: validation and extension

- **(A)** Paper data, 1961–2003 (reference)
- **(B)** New data, 1961–2003: validation
- **(C)** New data, 1961–`r end_year`: extension
- **(D)** As (C) without 2020–21 (COVID)
- **(E)** New data, 2004–`r end_year` only: out-of-sample

```{r ext-results}
min_years <- function(df, k = 20) {
  df |> group_by(iso3) |> filter(sum(!is.na(g)) >= k) |> ungroup()
}

run <- function(df, label) {
  m <- feols(g ~ tem + tem_poor + pre + pre_poor |
               iso3 + region^year + poor^year,
             data = df, cluster = ~ parent + region_year)
  pe <- poor_effect(m, "tem")
  data.frame(sample = label, rich = unname(coef(m)["tem"]),
             poor = pe["effect"], se_poor = pe["se"], p_poor = pe["p"],
             N = nobs(m), countries = n_distinct(df$iso3), row.names = NULL)
}

A <- est |>
  transmute(iso3, year, g, tem = wtem, pre = wpre, poor, region, parent,
            region_year, tem_poor = wtem_poor, pre_poor = wpre_poor)

res <- bind_rows(
  run(A,                                             "(A) Paper data 1961-2003"),
  run(min_years(filter(new, year <= 2003)),          "(B) New data 1961-2003"),
  run(min_years(new),                                paste0("(C) New data 1961-", end_year)),
  run(min_years(filter(new, !year %in% 2020:2021)),  "(D) (C) without 2020-21"),
  run(min_years(filter(new, year >= 2004), k = 15),  paste0("(E) New data 2004-", end_year))
)
res |> mutate(across(c(rich, poor, se_poor, p_poor), ~ round(.x, 3)))
```

Sample (E) covers only about 20 years, so the minimum is lowered to 15 years of data per country.

## 4.6 Has the effect changed over time? (adaptation)

Separate temperature effects per period in one pooled regression; the Wald test checks whether the poor-country effect is equal across periods.

```{r ext-adapt}
new_p <- min_years(new) |>
  mutate(period = cut(year, c(1960, 1979, 1999, end_year),
                      labels = c("1961-79", "1980-99", paste0("2000-", end_year))))
per <- levels(new_p$period)

period_effects <- function(m) {
  b <- coef(m); V <- vcov(m)
  do.call(rbind, lapply(per, function(p) {
    v1 <- paste0("period::", p, ":tem"); v2 <- paste0("period::", p, ":tem_poor")
    data.frame(period = p, poor_effect = unname(b[v1] + b[v2]),
               se = unname(sqrt(V[v1, v1] + V[v2, v2] + 2 * V[v1, v2])))
  }))
}

m_t <- feols(g ~ i(period, tem) + i(period, tem_poor) + pre + pre_poor |
               iso3 + region^year + poor^year,
             data = new_p, cluster = ~ parent + region_year)
period_effects(m_t)

# H0: same poor-country effect in all periods
b <- coef(m_t); V <- vcov(m_t)
R <- matrix(0, length(per) - 1, length(b), dimnames = list(NULL, names(b)))
for (k in 2:length(per)) {
  R[k - 1, paste0("period::", per[k], ":tem")]      <-  1
  R[k - 1, paste0("period::", per[k], ":tem_poor")] <-  1
  R[k - 1, paste0("period::", per[1], ":tem")]      <- -1
  R[k - 1, paste0("period::", per[1], ":tem_poor")] <- -1
}
dv <- R %*% b
W  <- as.numeric(t(dv) %*% solve(R %*% V %*% t(R)) %*% dv)
cat("Wald test: chi2(", nrow(R), ") =", round(W, 2),
    ", p =", round(pchisq(W, nrow(R), lower.tail = FALSE), 3), "\n")
```

### Balanced panel

Only countries observed in every period, so a change cannot come from countries entering later.

```{r ext-balanced}
bal_ids <- new_p |>
  filter(!is.na(g)) |>
  group_by(iso3) |>
  filter(n_distinct(period) == length(per)) |>
  pull(iso3) |> unique()

m_bal <- update(m_t, data = filter(new_p, iso3 %in% bal_ids))
period_effects(m_bal) |> mutate(countries = length(bal_ids))
```

## 4.7 Rolling 20-year windows (for the website)

```{r ext-rolling}
starts <- 1961:(end_year - 19)
roll <- do.call(rbind, lapply(starts, function(s) {
  r <- tryCatch(run(min_years(filter(new, year >= s, year <= s + 19), k = 15), ""),
                error = function(e) NULL)
  if (is.null(r)) return(NULL)
  data.frame(window_start = s, window_end = s + 19, poor = r$poor,
             lo = r$poor - 1.96 * r$se_poor, hi = r$poor + 1.96 * r$se_poor)
}))
write.csv(roll, "rolling_poor_effect.csv", row.names = FALSE)

fig_roll <- ggplot(roll, aes(window_end, poor)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed") +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = lo, ymax = hi), alpha = 0.2) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1) +
  labs(x = "Last year of 20-year window",
       y = "Effect of +1°C on growth in poor countries (pp)",
       title = "Temperature effect on growth in poor countries, rolling 20-year windows") +
  theme_minimal()
fig_roll
```

# 5. Outputs for the report (Problem Set 3)

Everything below is saved to the folder `output/`: LaTeX tables (for `\input{}` in the template) and PDF figures (for `\includegraphics{}`).

```{r out-folder}
dir.create("output", showWarnings = FALSE)
```

## 5.1 Section "Data": descriptive statistics (≈ paper's Table 1)

The paper's Table 1 shows how much temperature still varies *after* the fixed effects are removed. This is the variation that identifies β, and it is also the key number for the measurement-error argument in section (d).

```{r out-desc}
# Standard deviation of temperature/precipitation after removing FE step by step
resid_sd <- function(v, fe) sd(resid(feols(as.formula(paste(v, "~ 1 |", fe)), est)))
desc_var <- data.frame(
  variable = c("Temperature (°C)", "Precipitation (100 mm/yr)"),
  raw            = c(sd(est$wtem), sd(est$wpre)),
  country_FE     = c(resid_sd("wtem", "fips60_06"), resid_sd("wpre", "fips60_06")),
  plus_year_FE   = c(resid_sd("wtem", "fips60_06 + year"), resid_sd("wpre", "fips60_06 + year")),
  plus_region_yr = c(resid_sd("wtem", "fips60_06 + region^year + poor^year"),
                     resid_sd("wpre", "fips60_06 + region^year + poor^year"))
)
desc_var |> mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~ round(.x, 3)))

# Share of temperature variance left after all fixed effects
cat("Share of temperature variance left after the paper's FE:",
    round(desc_var$plus_region_yr[1]^2 / desc_var$raw[1]^2, 3), "\n")

# Summary statistics by income group
desc_grp <- est |>
  mutate(group = ifelse(poor == 1, "Poor", "Rich")) |>
  group_by(group) |>
  summarise(countries = n_distinct(fips60_06), obs = n(),
            growth_mean = mean(g), growth_sd = sd(g),
            temp_mean = mean(wtem), temp_sd = sd(wtem),
            precip_mean = mean(wpre), precip_sd = sd(wpre))
desc_grp |> mutate(across(where(is.double), ~ round(.x, 2)))

write.csv(desc_var, "output/desc_variation.csv", row.names = FALSE)
write.csv(desc_grp, "output/desc_by_group.csv",  row.names = FALSE)
```

## 5.2 Section "Main result": regression table as LaTeX

```{r out-table2}
etable(m1, m2, m3, m4,
       dict = c(g = "Annual GDP p.c. growth (pp)",
                wtem = "Temperature", wtem_poor = "Temperature $\\times$ Poor",
                wpre = "Precipitation", wpre_poor = "Precipitation $\\times$ Poor",
                wtem_hot = "Temperature $\\times$ Hot", wpre_hot = "Precipitation $\\times$ Hot",
                fips60_06 = "Country", region = "Region", poor = "Poor"),
       digits = 3, signif.code = c("***" = .01, "**" = .05, "*" = .10),
       extralines = list("Temp. effect, poor countries" =
                           c("", sprintf("%.3f (%.3f)",
                             c(poor_effect(m2, "wtem")["effect"], poor_effect(m3, "wtem")["effect"],
                               poor_effect(m4, "wtem")["effect"]),
                             c(poor_effect(m2, "wtem")["se"], poor_effect(m3, "wtem")["se"],
                               poor_effect(m4, "wtem")["se"])))),
       tex = TRUE, file = "output/table2_replication.tex", replace = TRUE)
cat("Saved output/table2_replication.tex\n")
```

## 5.3 Section "Main result": figures

**Figure A**, the replication of the paper's Figure 1: each country's temperature range (grey spike, min–max), its 1950s mean and its 1996–2005 mean, against log GDP per capita in 2000. Shows that hot countries are poor (the cross-sectional correlation the paper does *not* rely on) and that every country experiences substantial year-to-year variation (the variation it does rely on).

```{r out-fig1, fig.width = 8, fig.height = 5}
f1 <- read_dta("climate_panel.dta") |>
  group_by(fips60_06, country_code) |>
  summarise(lngdp2000 = log(rgdpl[year == 2000][1]),
            tmin = min(wtem, na.rm = TRUE), tmax = max(wtem, na.rm = TRUE),
            t50s = mean(wtem[year >= 1950 & year <= 1959], na.rm = TRUE),
            t00s = mean(wtem[year >= 1996 & year <= 2005], na.rm = TRUE),
            .groups = "drop") |>
  filter(is.finite(lngdp2000), fips60_06 %in% unique(est$fips60_06))

fig1 <- ggplot(f1, aes(lngdp2000)) +
  geom_linerange(aes(ymin = tmin, ymax = tmax), colour = "grey75") +
  geom_point(aes(y = t50s, colour = "Mean 1950-1959"), shape = 1, size = 1.8) +
  geom_point(aes(y = t00s, colour = "Mean 1996-2005"), shape = 3, size = 1.8) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c("Mean 1950-1959" = "blue", "Mean 1996-2005" = "red"), name = NULL) +
  labs(x = "Log GDP per capita in 2000 (PPP)", y = "Temperature (°C, population-weighted)",
       title = "Temperature levels and variation by income") +
  theme_minimal() + theme(legend.position = "bottom")
fig1
ggsave("output/fig1_temperature_income.pdf", fig1, width = 8, height = 5)
```

**Figure B**, the main result: effect in poor vs. rich countries (from section 2.4).

## 5.4 Section "Critical evaluation": supporting numbers

### (a) Measurement error: correcting attenuation with IV

With two independent noisy measures of the same true temperature, one can instrument one with the other (Topic 2b + 2c): if the errors are classical and independent, IV removes the attenuation bias. Here the paper's temperature (Matsuura & Willmott) is instrumented with CRU temperature, 1961–2003.

Caveat for the report: both datasets are built from largely the same weather stations, so their errors are probably *correlated*. Then IV only partly removes the bias, i.e. the IV estimate is a lower bound (in absolute value) for the error-corrected effect.

```{r out-iv}
cru_iso <- cru_w |> select(iso3, year, tem_cru = tem, pre_cru = pre)
iv_dat <- est |>
  left_join(cru_iso, by = c("iso3", "year")) |>
  filter(!is.na(tem_cru)) |>
  mutate(tem_cru_poor = tem_cru * poor)

m_ols_iv_sample <- feols(g ~ wtem + wtem_poor | fips60_06 + region^year + poor^year,
                         iv_dat, cluster = cl)
m_iv <- feols(g ~ 1 | fips60_06 + region^year + poor^year |
                wtem + wtem_poor ~ tem_cru + tem_cru_poor,
              iv_dat, cluster = cl)

round(rbind("OLS (same sample)"                     = poor_effect(m_ols_iv_sample, "wtem"),
            "IV: paper temp. instrumented by CRU"   = poor_effect(m_iv, "fit_wtem")), 3)

# First stage strength (should be far above 10)
fitstat(m_iv, "ivwald")
```

### (b) Growth or level effect? Lagged temperature (≈ paper's Table 3)

If a hot year only lowers the *level* of output (e.g. a bad harvest), growth recovers afterwards and the sum of current and lagged effects goes back towards zero. If the cumulative effect stays negative, temperature affects the *growth rate*. The paper argues for the latter.

```{r out-lags}
est <- est |>
  arrange(fips60_06, year) |>
  group_by(fips60_06) |>
  # lag k of temperature, only if the year k years earlier is in the data (no gaps)
  mutate(L1_wtem = ifelse(lag(year, 1) == year - 1, lag(wtem, 1), NA),
         L2_wtem = ifelse(lag(year, 2) == year - 2, lag(wtem, 2), NA),
         L3_wtem = ifelse(lag(year, 3) == year - 3, lag(wtem, 3), NA),
         L4_wtem = ifelse(lag(year, 4) == year - 4, lag(wtem, 4), NA),
         L5_wtem = ifelse(lag(year, 5) == year - 5, lag(wtem, 5), NA)) |>
  ungroup() |>
  mutate(across(L1_wtem:L5_wtem, ~ .x * poor, .names = "{.col}_poor"))

cum_poor <- function(nl) {
  v  <- c("wtem", if (nl > 0) paste0("L", 1:nl, "_wtem"))
  vp <- paste0(v, "_poor")
  m  <- feols(as.formula(paste("g ~", paste(c(v, vp), collapse = " + "),
                               "| fips60_06 + region^year + poor^year")), est, cluster = cl)
  a  <- setNames(rep(0, length(coef(m))), names(coef(m))); a[c(v, vp)] <- 1
  e  <- sum(a * coef(m)); se <- sqrt(as.numeric(t(a) %*% vcov(m) %*% a))
  data.frame(lags = nl, cumulative_poor = e, se = se, p = 2 * pnorm(-abs(e / se)), N = nobs(m))
}
lag_tab <- do.call(rbind, lapply(c(0, 1, 3, 5), cum_poor))
lag_tab |> mutate(across(c(cumulative_poor, se, p), ~ round(.x, 3)))
write.csv(lag_tab, "output/lags_cumulative.csv", row.names = FALSE)
```

### (c) Inference: how sensitive are the standard errors to the clustering choice?

Weather is spatially correlated, so errors of neighbouring countries in the same year are likely correlated. The table shows the poor-country effect from column 3 with different standard errors.

```{r out-se}
se_tab <- do.call(rbind, lapply(list(
  "Heteroskedasticity-robust only"          = "hetero",
  "Clustered by country"                    = ~ fips60_06,
  "Clustered by region × year"              = ~ region_year,
  "Two-way: parent & region × year (paper)" = ~ parent + region_year,
  "Two-way: country & year"                 = ~ fips60_06 + year
), function(v) {
  pe <- poor_effect(summary(m3, vcov = v), "wtem")
  data.frame(effect = pe["effect"], se = pe["se"], p = pe["p"])
}))
se_tab |> mutate(across(everything(), ~ round(.x, 3)))
write.csv(se_tab, "output/se_clustering.csv")
```
